text:
Emily: quick heads-up — I'm opening a tiny docs PR for the metering + pricing page. wording around how 'overages' and soft rate-limits are attributed to tiers is confusing in prod examples :grimacing:
Kevin: thanks — can you point to the exact paragraph and paste the example you're planning to replace? :eyes:
Emily: sure. current text says:
```
When a request exceeds the soft limit, it will be counted toward the higher tier for that billing window.
```
Which reads like it always moves the whole request count to that tier. I think we intended: only the overage tokens are billed at the overage tier, and dashboard panels should reflect split attribution.
Nora: yeah this lines up with what I saw in the analytics — the panel aggregates by "tier attribution" and we tag token usage with headers so attribution is per-token not per-request. docs still references "plan-level switch" (old wording).
Emily: right. I'm proposing we update copy + add a tiny SDK curl/python snippet and a dashboard note. Draft curl snippet I'm adding to the PR: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tier: pro" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Say hi"}'
```
And python: 
```python
import requests
headers = {
  "Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}",
  "X-Redwood-Tier": "pro",
}
requests.post("https://api.redwood.com/v1/complete", json={"prompt":"hi"}, headers=headers)
```
Kevin: nice — two notes: (1) prefer header name X-Redwood-Client-Tier in v2 (we renamed in the API change last quarter), (2) can we avoid implying header is required for correct billing? it's optional and used to override attribution for multi-tenant frontends.
Emily: good catch — I'll update to X-Redwood-Client-Tier and add a short sentence: "Optional header used to attribute usage for multi-tenant billing. If omitted, attribution defaults to the API key's tier."
Sam: also add a tiny screenshot note for the dashboard: "Panel shows split by 'default' vs 'override' when Client-Tier header is used" — that helped our support tickets.
Nora: there's a broken link in the sidebar: /billing/tiers -> should be /pricing/tiers. docs-ci-bot flagged it in my local link check.
docs-ci-bot: Link check — 1 broken link found in docs/metering.md: /billing/tiers -> suggested /pricing/tiers.
Emily: thanks, I'll patch that. Also adding a short regression test: update the usage-e2e snippet in docs-tests to assert the dashboard link resolves.
Kevin: can you also include a short note on how rate-limit fallback affects attribution? i.e., when a request is routed to a lower-capacity pool and model variant changes, tokens should still attribute to original tier unless overridden. That prevents confusion when folks see model variance in logs but the billing panel shows same tier attribution.
Emily: okay — short paragraph + inline example to clarify. I'll push changes shortly. Assigning @Sam for docs review and @Nora for analytics wording.
Sam: I'll review in the morning, prefer concise language. If we change header name, add a tiny migration note: "Old header X-Plan previously used; v2 uses X-Redwood-Client-Tier".
Nora: Can we also add an SDK snippet for node? small code: 
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/complete', {method: 'POST', headers: {authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}`, 'X-Redwood-Client-Tier': 'pro'}, body: JSON.stringify({prompt: 'hi'})})
```
Emily: adding node snippet and the migration note. I'll also update the dashboard panel caption and add a tiny note in the changelog section of metering.md.
Kevin: cool. once PR is up, ping me and I'll sanity-check the billing phrasing. :thumbsup:
Emily: PR opened: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/docs/pull/918 — includes copy + curl/python/node snippets + link fix + test update. cc @Kevin @Nora
Sam: reviewing now. small nit: replace "overage tier" with "overage rate" in one spot for clarity.
Emily: thanks — fixed. pushed a new commit.
Sam: LGTM, sending approval. :white_check_mark:
Emily: merging after CI passes. thanks everyone! :rocket:
